Grays Harbor Recreational Crab Harvest Estimate

Gear-Resolved CPUE Model (cross-check) - 2025-26 Season (2025-09-16 to 2026-09-15)

Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

2026-10-19

How to read this report. This is the results report for one seasonal harvest estimate from the gear-resolved CPUE model. Code is hidden by default; use the Code buttons (or Code > Show All Code at the top right) to reveal any step. Each section states what it does, shows the notable tables and figures, and, for the diagnostic sections, notes what a healthy run should look like. The headline number is the port total in the Results section; always read it together with the convergence and PE-vs-BSS sections, which say how much to trust it. This model is the independent cross-check on the pooled CPUE model; the two should agree on the boat and the port total.

1. Setup, configuration, and inputs

Loads packages, sources the helper functions in 03_R_functions/, applies the run configuration from run_config.R (the single file of user toggles), builds the pot-closure sub-seasons, defines the PE / BSS / census estimators, and reads the season effort counts, crabber interviews, commercial tally, and ingress/egress surveys. Nothing here is a result; it is the machinery every later section uses.

###############################################################################
# Crab Creel Estimation - Westport / Grays Harbor  |  Gear-Resolved CPUE Model
# Framework v6.0 (2026-09-12)  |  the season(s) run_config.R selects
#
# Estimates total recreational Dungeness crab harvest at Westport / Grays Harbor
# with a per-gear-type CPUE process (shared AR(1) dynamics), so gear-type catch can
# carry posterior uncertainty. Three population components (shore, private boat, and
# commercial/charter census) across two gear-regime sub-seasons: the pot closure
# (Sep 16 - Nov 30 on 2024-25, no pots, non-pot gear only) and all-gear (Dec 1 - Sep 15), with
# per-population periods from gear_period_bss (since A32: shore all-gear weekly, boat all-gear
# monthly, both pot-closure fits biweekly).
#
# STATE AT v5.6 (v6.0 since 2026-09-12 carries it forward): both shore and boat run on the gear-DEPLOYMENT effort unit
# (h = number_of_gear, L = tau), via the shared 03_R_functions/bss_effort_spec.R.
# Helper functions live in 03_R_functions/ (sourced wholesale in the setup chunk),
# and every user-selectable toggle lives in run_config.R (the single file you edit);
# this .Rmd's params block holds only model-internal tuning. NOTE: as driven G = 1,
# so the per-gear CPUE machinery is inert and gear-type catch is PE-apportioned
# (backlog item GR-7, "Option A").
#
# KEY FEATURES: weighted fractional gear-type classification; pi_gear as data
# (period x day_type, Laplace-smoothed); per-gear process error and overdispersion;
# B1 weekend + B2 holiday effort effects; B1_C weekend CPUE effect (estimate_B1_C);
# gear-deployment effort scale (R_G_boat / tau); commercial CENSUS over the tally days plus
# a vessel-stratified charter EXPANSION with a finite-population correction (2026-09-11;
# this line said "day-type-stratified commercial / charter census expansion" until
# 2026-09-12, which is the retired estimator). Framework v6.0 on the Method v2.0
# configuration: dynamic per-stratum crabbing fraction f, derived shore turnover,
# calibration boat turnover with a shared tau_bar. The zero-inflated catch block has been in
# this track's Stan model since 2026-09-13 (the D6 port) and ships ON for the shore fits since
# 2026-10-02 (A32; catch_zi_tracks = c("pooled", "gear_resolved")). Every chain starts with init_r = run_config$bss_init_r (0.5, B51).
#
# FULL CHANGE LOG (framework v5.x, the F/P fix-markers, and the GR backlog):
#   07_documentation/BSS-GH-gear-type-CPUE-model-development-history.md
# METHOD REFERENCE:
#   07_documentation/BSS-GH-gear-type-CPUE-model-documentation.md
###############################################################################

# ===========================================================================
# 0. SETUP - Load packages and configure environment
# ===========================================================================

# 2026-09-28 (B46): one package list and loader (03_R_functions/bss_packages.R): renv.lock's
# versions when renv is active, a stop naming the package when one cannot be had.
if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Package 'here' is missing: run renv::restore() first.", call. = FALSE)
source(here::here("03_R_functions", "bss_packages.R")); bss_load_packages()
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
purrr::walk(list.files(here("03_R_functions"), full.names = TRUE), source)

# Create dated output directory. Unique per-run subfolder so same-day runs never
# overwrite each other. run_config$run_tag (set in run_config.R, or by
# run_rg_sweep.R) names the folder, e.g. gear-type-CPUE-model-run5; blank falls back
# to a HHMMSS timestamp. The `knit:` block above stashes that timestamp in
# options(crab_run_tag=) so a standalone RStudio knit keeps its HTML and this
# driver's CSVs in the SAME folder.
run_date <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")
# 2026-09-28 (B46): see bss_output_dir.R (no reuse of a filled folder, no mislabelled season).
output_dir <- bss_output_dir("gear-type-CPUE-model-", if (exists("run_config")) run_config else NULL)


# --- Timing ---
# timer_start() / timer_stop() and their timing state now live in
# 03_R_functions/bss_timers.R (auto-sourced). Read collected timings with
# bss_timer_log(). Extracted; behavior unchanged.

run_start_time <- Sys.time()

# ===========================================================================
# 0.1 PARAMETERS - All user-configurable settings in one place
# ===========================================================================

params <- list(
  # NOTE: every user-selectable toggle (season window, structural dates, catch
  # groups, day-typing, effort unit, incomplete-trip filter, I/E settings,
  # holidays, and the model-behavior levers estimate_B1_C / ar_adaptive /
  # loo_effort_unit_comparison / use_boat_ie) now lives in run_config.R, the single
  # source of truth, and is applied as an override below. This list holds ONLY this
  # model's internal tuning: the Stan model file, per-fit sampler settings, the
  # convergence-gate thresholds, the AR-selector thresholds, and a few gear-model
  # constants. These rarely change and legitimately differ from the pooled model.

  # --- Stan model file ---
  bss_model_file    = "crab_bss_gear_resolved.stan",

  # --- Shared reader behavior (merged fetch_crab_data, 2026-08-01) ---
  # FALSE reproduces the former fetch_crab_data_v2: keep private_boat interviews
  # regardless of gear_time_total (the pooled reader drops boats with no positive
  # gear-time). Behavior-neutral for this track vs the pre-merge _v2 reader.
  boat_require_gear_time = FALSE,

  # --- Default BSS period (overridden per fit by gear_period_bss: per population since A32) ---
  period_bss        = "month",

  # --- BSS sampler settings ---
  bss_max_interviews = NULL,  # v5.1: use full dataset (was 1000)

  bss_iter_default          = 2000,
  bss_warmup_default        = 1000,
  bss_max_treedepth_default = 10,
  bss_adapt_delta_default   = 0.9,

  # Per-fit overrides. The shore all-gear fit has 4 gear types across 43 weekly
  # periods since A32 (10 monthly before) with 1,600+ interviews (the most complex posterior geometry): more
  # iterations, higher adapt_delta, and a deeper treedepth to avoid trajectory
  # truncation (93.9% saturation at max_treedepth=10). Pot-closure fits are data-sparse
  # and benefit from tighter adaptation. Boat all-gear was added 2026-09-02; see below.
  bss_iter_shore_allgear    = 4000,
  bss_warmup_shore_allgear  = 2000,
  bss_treedepth_shore_allgear = 14,
  bss_delta_shore_allgear     = 0.95,

  bss_iter_ringnet          = 4000,
  bss_warmup_ringnet        = 2000,
  bss_treedepth_ringnet     = 12,
  bss_delta_ringnet         = 0.95,

  # --- Boat all-gear (2026-09-02). THIS FIT HAD NO PER-FIT OVERRIDE AND COULD NOT SAMPLE. ---
  # Until now shore-all-gear and both pot-closure fits had explicit settings and private_boat
  # all-gear fell through to the track defaults (2,000/1,000, adapt_delta 0.90, treedepth 10).
  # On the same data and the same component the POOLED track runs 5,000/2,500 at adapt_delta
  # 0.99 / treedepth 13 and gets 39 divergences; this track got 554, tau_bar n_eff 49, R-hat
  # 1.0813, and the convergence gate REJECTED the fit, so the component fell back to PE and
  # the gear-resolved port total read 51,385 instead of about 70,900 - a 27% understatement
  # of the cross-check that validates the pooled headline.
  #
  # The 2026-08-30 Stage 5 batch demonstrated the fix (stage S3): with these settings the same
  # fit returns 2 divergences, tau_bar n_eff 19,292, R-hat 0.9997, and passes the gate, and the
  # two tracks then agree on tau_bar to 0.03%. That demonstration lived in an EXPERIMENT-ONLY
  # override (bss_sampler_override), so production never got it, and the 2026-09-01 validation
  # batch reproduced the failure exactly (554 divergences, n_eff 49, bit-identical to the
  # 2026-08-29 run). Moving the settings here is the permanent fix.
  #
  # Draw count alone would NOT have worked: n_eff 49 on 4,000 post-warmup draws is 1.2%
  # efficiency, so reaching the gate's floor of 400 by draws would need about 32,000. Raising
  # draws 2.5x raised n_eff 394x, which is the signature of adaptation, not of sample size.
  bss_iter_boat_allgear       = 5000,
  bss_warmup_boat_allgear     = 2500,
  bss_treedepth_boat_allgear  = 13,
  bss_delta_boat_allgear      = 0.99,

  # bss_min_interviews MOVED to run_config.R (improvement 6, 2026-08-25). It lived here,
  # in params_model, which is merged ON TOP of run_config -- so a value set in run_config
  # was silently overridden. Both the pre-filter floor (bss_min_interviews) and the new
  # post-filter floor (bss_min_interviews_fitted) are now single-sourced from run_config.R.

  # --- Minimum effective-N per gear type for independent modeling ---
  # Gear types with fewer than this many effective interviews (sum of fractional
  # weights) are collapsed. Raised from 3 to 15 because fractional weights from
  # multi-gear interviews can push phantom gear types above a low threshold.
  bss_min_gear_effective_n = 15,

  # --- R_G fixed value for boat fits (Issue 5) ---
  R_G_fixed_boat = 1.3,

  # (ie_min_obs_boat moved to run_config.R only, 2026-09-28, B46: a key in both lists is
  # decided silently by this one, so editing run_config's value changed nothing.)

  # --- Project centroid (Westport), used for the civil-twilight computation ---
  centroid_lat = 46.904,
  centroid_lon = -124.105,
  local_tz     = "America/Los_Angeles",

  # (D37, 2026-09-29: the v5.2 count-based max_divergences key was removed; the
  #  scale-aware gate below superseded it and nothing read it.)

  # --- B1.8 scale-aware convergence gate (ported from pooled) -----------------
  # A fit passes only if R-hat/n_eff pass AND the divergence fraction is below
  # max_divergence_fraction AND the divergences do not move the reported totals by
  # more than max_divergence_total_impact_sd (in posterior-SD units).
  max_divergence_total_impact_sd = 0.10,
  max_divergence_fraction        = 0.05,

  # --- AR temporal-resolution thresholds (selector: 03_R_functions/bss_ar_resolution.R) ---
  # The per-model AR cap map now lives in run_config.R (ar_max_resolution$gear_resolved);
  # this model's cap is selected from it just after the merge below (P5, 2026-07-12).
  # It is used only when ar_adaptive = TRUE (see run_config); production gear-resolved
  # is ar_adaptive = FALSE (fixed period_bss), so the cap is dormant. The map is
  # conservative because the gear-resolved latent AR is P_n x (G*S): with 4 gear types
  # a daily AR is ~4x the pooled latent dimension at the same P_n.
  ar_daily_min_coverage  = 0.25,
  ar_daily_min_obs       = 20,
  ar_weekly_min_per_week = 1.5
)

# --- Run-level config from run_config.R (single source of truth) --------------
# run_config.R owns every user-selectable toggle (season window, structural dates,
# catch groups, day-typing, effort unit, filters, I/E settings, holidays, the AR
# resolution map, and the model-behavior toggles). When launched via run_estimation.R
# the orchestrator has already defined `run_config`; when this .Rmd is knit standalone
# the guard below sources run_config.R so the same toggles are used either way.
if (!exists("run_config")) source(here::here("run_config.R"))
# P5 (2026-07-12): run_config is the BASE parameter set; this model's internal tuning
# (defined above) is layered on top. The two key sets are disjoint, so the merge order
# carries intent only (run_config is the base, the model updates it with its specifics).
params <- modifyList(run_config, params)
# 2026-08-30: the ONE sanctioned way for run_config to reach a sampler setting, applied
# AFTER the merge because params_model wins it (03_R_functions/bss_sampler_override.R).
# Unset in production, so this is a no-op on a normal run; it errors loudly on a
# non-sampler key rather than silently dropping it.
params <- bss_apply_sampler_override(params, model_label = "gear_resolved")
# Select this model's AR-resolution cap from the shared per-model map in run_config.
params$ar_max_resolution <- run_config$ar_max_resolution$gear_resolved

# Crabbing holidays now live in an editable workbook (04_input_files/crabbing_holidays.xlsx),
# read here via 03_R_functions/read_crabbing_holidays.R and filtered to season_filter, so the
# season update is a spreadsheet edit rather than a code edit. Populate params$crabbing_holiday_dates
# ONCE here; every downstream consumer (classify_day_type, prep_days_crab, estimate_comm_charter)
# reads it from params unchanged. Kept as a bare object too so inline references still resolve.
params$crabbing_holiday_dates <- read_crabbing_holidays(params)
crabbing_holiday_dates <- params$crabbing_holiday_dates

# --- Derived: catch groups vector used throughout ---
# Dungeness only. The Red Rock catch group and its estimate_red_rock switch were removed
# 2026-09-28 (B44): never shipped on, and never validated (turning it on summed the two
# species in the monthly tables). The loops over catch_groups stay, over one group.
catch_groups <- "Dungeness_Kept"

# --- Derived: sub-season date ranges (03_R_functions/build_subseasons.R) --------
# Split by the pot-closure window (params$pot_closure_start / pot_closure_end, added
# 2026-07-13). Each sub-season carries its own BSS period type (biweekly for the pot
# closure: fewer months, sparse data; monthly for all-gear), and since A32 gear_period_bss's
# per-population form overrides it per fit (shore all-gear weekly) and the gear types excluded
# by regulation. During the closure Pot is excluded: pots are illegal Sep 16 - Nov 30,
# and stray "Pot" mentions in that window are recording errors (crabbers naming gear
# they own, not what they deployed); fitting a Pot CPUE process with <6 fractional
# interviews causes catastrophic convergence failure (divergences, overflow in
# C_sum_gear). For the current config (closure at the season start) this returns the
# historical two sub-seasons with unchanged internal names ("ring_net_only" is the pot-
# closure key, kept for output-filename continuity; display_name is "Pot closure"), so
# keys and filenames do not change. The name "ring-net only" was a misnomer: non-pot
# gear other than ring nets is also legal in the closure. Model logic keys off
# ss$gear_regime ("pot_closure" | "all_gear"), never ss$name.
subseasons <- build_subseasons(params)
for (ss in subseasons) {
  message(sprintf("Sub-season: %-28s %s to %s (%d days, periods=%s)\n",
              paste0(ss$display_name, " [", ss$name, "]"),
              ss$start, ss$end, as.integer(ss$end - ss$start + 1), ss$period_bss))
}
message(sprintf("Catch groups: %s\n", paste(catch_groups, collapse = ", ")))
# Sub-season aggregation is now GENERAL (2026-07-13): the PE port summary, the catch-by-
# mode table, and the final harvest summary sum over whatever sub-seasons build_subseasons
# produced (via pe_pop_sum / pe_port_total below), rather than the hardcoded historical
# pair. A mid-season pot closure (which adds all_gear_pre / all_gear_post keys) is
# therefore handled end-to-end. That general path has NOT yet been validated against a
# fitted run, so emit a loud note when the sub-season set departs from the historical
# pair; verify the port total against the per-component PE table before citing such a run.
ss_name_set <- vapply(subseasons, function(z) z$name, character(1))
if (!setequal(ss_name_set, c("ring_net_only", "all_gear"))) {
  message(sprintf(paste0(
    "\n*** NOTE: non-historical sub-season set {%s}. The report aggregation sums over all ",
    "sub-seasons per population, but this configuration has not been validated against a ",
    "fitted run; verify the port total against the per-component PE table before citing. ***\n"),
    paste(ss_name_set, collapse = ", ")))
}

# --- Generalized PE aggregation over the sub-season set (build_subseasons) -----------
# Sum a PE field over all sub-seasons of a population so the port total, the by-mode
# table, and the final harvest summary follow build_subseasons instead of a fixed 5-row
# layout. These close over the run globals `pe_all` (populated by the PE loop) and
# `subseasons`; they are only called after the PE loop, so pe_all exists by call time.
# pe_all keys are "<population>_<subseason-name>"; a missing key or field contributes 0.
pe_field   <- function(key, field) pe_all[[key]][[field]] %||% 0
pe_pop_sum <- function(pop, field)
  sum(vapply(subseasons, function(ss) pe_field(paste0(pop, "_", ss$name), field), numeric(1)), na.rm = TRUE)
pe_port_total <- function(field)  # na.rm matches the baseline sum([1:5], na.rm=TRUE):
  sum(pe_pop_sum("shore", field), pe_pop_sum("private_boat", field),
      pe_field("comm_charter", field), na.rm = TRUE)

# Pot-closure boundary markers for date-axis plots (see the pooled driver for the
# rationale). Dotted line at the closure start, dashed line at the day pots open
# (closure end + 1), so every season plot brackets the pot-closure window. Returns a
# list of ggplot layers added with `+`; labels = FALSE draws the lines only.
pot_closure_markers <- function(params, labels = TRUE) {
  pc_start  <- as.Date(params$pot_closure_start %||% params$est_date_start)
  pots_open <- as.Date(params$pot_open_date     %||% (as.Date(params$pot_closure_end) + 1))
  layers <- list(
    geom_vline(xintercept = pc_start,  linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.5),
    geom_vline(xintercept = pots_open, linetype = "dashed", color = "red",       linewidth = 0.5))
  if (labels) layers <- c(layers, list(
    annotate("text", x = pc_start + 3,  y = Inf, label = "Pot closure start",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "darkgreen"),
    annotate("text", x = pots_open + 3, y = Inf, label = "Pots open",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "red")))
  layers
}

# ---- 7.0 LOAD DATA ----
timer_start("1_load_data")
message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n LOADING DATA\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
dwg <- fetch_crab_data(params)
## Reading data...
##   Grays Harbor interviews by population:
##     comm_charter: 80 
##     private_boat: 1251 
##     shore: 4963 
##   Private-boat contacts for the crabbing fraction (Westport Boat Launch + Ocean Shores Boat Launch): 1024 boats on 81 days, 246 crabbing (share 0.240); trip type on 1024, of which 111 crab-only, 135 combo, 709 other fishery, 69 non-fishing

##   Charter roster (Westport): 11 trips on 11 days; 6 interviewed, 2 missed, 3 canceled
##

##   Boat effort obs: 463 (221 days)

##

##   2025-26    data 2025-09-16 to 2026-09-08 | in window: 1463 effort counts, 5085 interviews | outside 0
# --- Ingress/egress data + L_effective model (shared with the pooled driver) ---
# fetch_ie_data() and estimate_L_effective() live in 03_R_functions/bss_day_length.R.
# L_eff_model is NULL when I/E data are absent or fewer than 3 shore days exist;
# prep_days_crab() then falls back to civil twilight and warns.
ie_data <- fetch_ie_data(params)
## 
##   Reading I/E data...
##   I/E survey days: 40 shore (WDF20), 2 boat (WBL)
##   Date range: 2023-08-17 to 2026-08-28
##   Shore L_effective: mean=5.5 hrs (range 2.7-7.7)
##   Crab-fraction I/E classification: 0 WBL rows, 0 total / 0 crab boats (f_hat = NA)
# Review item 1 (2026-09-08): the crabbing-fraction classification rows come from the
# sampler contacts (dwg$boat_contacts, every private boat approached) and/or the egress
# columns of the I/E workbook, per params$crab_fraction_source. See crab_fraction.R.
params$crab_fraction_rows <- crab_fraction_source_rows(dwg, ie_data, params)
##   Crab-fraction classification rows (source = both): interviews 81 days, 1024 boats, share 0.240
##     combo share of crabbing boats (typed contacts): 135 combo of 246 crabbing; by month: 2025-09 -, 2025-10 -, 2025-11 0.00 (n=2), 2025-12 0.00 (n=44), 2026-01 0.00 (n=24), 2026-02 0.00 (n=8), 2026-03 1.00 (n=1), 2026-04 0.92 (n=13), 2026-05 0.50 (n=4), 2026-06 0.67 (n=6), 2026-07 0.77 (n=64), 2026-08 0.84 (n=61), 2026-09 0.84 (n=19)
##     by month: 2025-09 0.00 (n=1), 2025-10 0.00 (n=1), 2025-11 0.67 (n=3), 2025-12 0.98 (n=45), 2026-01 0.83 (n=29), 2026-02 0.80 (n=10), 2026-03 0.20 (n=5), 2026-04 0.57 (n=23), 2026-05 0.40 (n=10), 2026-06 0.27 (n=22), 2026-07 0.16 (n=399), 2026-08 0.16 (n=386), 2026-09 0.21 (n=90)
# Review item 2 (2026-09-08): shore turnover at the count hours, derived every run from the
# I/E time column and adopted only under tau_shore_prior_mu = "derived". Mirrors the pooled
# driver; see 03_R_functions/bss_day_length.R (estimate_shore_turnover).
shore_turnover <- estimate_shore_turnover(attr(ie_data, "ie_intervals"), dwg$shore_effort, params)
##   Shore turnover derived from 40 I/E day(s) (ALL seasons pooled; the default); 17 of the 40 days in the workbook fall INSIDE the estimation window (2025-09-16 to 2026-09-15).
##   *** NOTE: only 42% of the I/E days behind this turnover are inside the window it is applied to. The shore component scales linearly in it; read sigma_IE in the fitted output, which is the in-window check. ***
##   Shore turnover from the I/E time column: 40 days; arrivals / presence at the season's count hours = 2.516 (ratio of sums; geometric mean of daily ratios 2.656; between-day log-SD 0.33; bootstrap log-SE 0.042). Peak-based value (the pre-2026-09-08 prior): 1.669.
##     presence at the count hours averages 0.65 of the daily peak; weekday 2.50 / weekend 2.53
##     IN-WINDOW SUBSET: 17 of 40 day(s), ratio of sums 2.595 against 2.516 pooled. The pooled value is what ships; tau_shore_derive_window_only = TRUE uses the subset.
write_shore_turnover(shore_turnover, output_dir)
params <- bss_resolve_tau_shore_prior(params, shore_turnover)
##   tau_shore prior centre RESOLVED from the I/E time column: 2.516 (40 days); shore shared-turnover floor waived.
##   tau_shore prior log-SD RESOLVED: 0.100 (bootstrap log-SE 0.042, floor 0.10).
# --- 2026-09-09: the sampler shifts and the shift-coverage diagnostic. The crabbing
# fraction is read from boats contacted DURING a shift (about 9:45 to 15:50); this writes
# how much of the day's boat returns the shift covers (from the boat I/E return profile)
# and whether the trip-type mix drifts with the hour inside the shift. Diagnostic only;
# guarded so a missing shifts file cannot break a run (03_R_functions/sampler_shifts.R).
sampler_shifts <- tryCatch(fetch_sampler_shifts(params),
                           error = function(e) { cat("  Sampler shifts skipped:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
##   Sampler shifts: 292 surveys on 221 days in the window (0 flagged and held out of the hours); check-in median 09:46, check-out median 15:50
shift_coverage <- tryCatch(diagnose_shift_coverage(sampler_shifts, ie_data, dwg$boat_contacts_detail, params, output_dir = output_dir),
                           error = function(e) { cat("  Shift coverage diagnostic skipped:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
##   Shift coverage: 221 shift days; in port 09:45 to 15:51 (medians), 6.1 h; the boat return profile (all boat-I/E sites pooled (WBL has 5 days, floor 10)) puts 76% of a day's returns inside the shift (9% before the first check-in, 15% after the last check-out)
##     contact hour by trip type (median [q25, q75]): combo 13:21 [12:03, 14:38] n=135; crab_only 12:38 [10:54, 14:03] n=111; non_fishing 11:52 [10:27, 13:25] n=69; other_fishery 13:01 [11:40, 14:19] n=709
##     crabbing share of typed contacts by hour bin: 08-10 0.34 (n=38), 10-12 0.21 (n=299), 12-14 0.24 (n=374), 14-16 0.26 (n=303), 16-18 0.10 (n=10)
# --- Phase 0/1b: OSP Westport boat-count ingest + overlap calibration (diagnostic) ---
# Mirrors the pooled driver. fetch_osp_boat_counts() + diagnose_osp_trailer_overlap()
# live in 03_R_functions/ (auto-sourced); the diagnostic writes its CSVs + plot to
# output_dir. Guarded so a missing file cannot break a run. The gear-resolved boat fit
# consumes OSP via prep_bss_crab_gear() when use_osp_boat_counts = TRUE (Phase 1b).
# D41 (c), 2026-10-19, as the pooled driver: an ingest ERROR under use_osp_boat_counts = TRUE
# stops the run here with its cause (the boat prep stopped on it anyway); the prep reads the
# series from params. A window with no OSP day is an empty series, not an error.
osp_boat <- tryCatch(fetch_osp_boat_counts(params), error = function(e) {
  if (isTRUE(params$use_osp_boat_counts))
    stop("OSP ingest failed: ", conditionMessage(e),
         "\n  use_osp_boat_counts = TRUE makes the OSP boat count (A30) and its crab-only share (A33) part of the method; ",
         "fix the input (04_input_files/WBL_boat_counts.xlsx, osp_sampling_rates.xlsx) or set use_osp_boat_counts = FALSE ",
         "to run without them, which is a different method.", call. = FALSE)
  bss_warn("OSP", paste("OSP ingest skipped (use_osp_boat_counts = FALSE):", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
## 
##   Reading OSP Westport boat-launch counts...
##   OSP boat-count days in window: 23 (1 observed zeros); range 2025-09-17 to 2025-10-18
##   NS handling: absent dates are NON-SAMPLED (latent, imputed by the AR); observed zeros are kept as data.
##   NOTE: 9 OSP day(s) with boats (106 returning in all) carry no crab-only value and are read as UNCLASSIFIED and dropped (osp_absent_day = "unclassified"; D39: if they are zero days the fitted crab-only share is biased up under "unclassified"; the question is with OSP; osp_absent_days.csv lists them) 
##   OSP sampling: the crab-only share is out of 173 SAMPLED boats (of 188 returning); n from schedule (minimum rate) on 13 day(s).
##   NOTE: days on the schedule take the manual's MINIMUM rate; OSP may have sampled above it, so on
##         those days n is a lower bound and the crab-only share an upper bound. Deliver the day's rate
##         (osp_sample_rate_col) or the number sampled (osp_crab_checked_col) to remove this.
##   NOTE: OSP crab-only share: on 13 of 13 OSP day(s) n is the manual's MINIMUM sampling rate (no daily rate or sampled count delivered), so there n is a lower bound and the share an UPPER bound on the truth (D2); osp_sampling_rate_source = "none" (every boat sampled) is the bound in the other direction 
##   OSP crab-only classification: 13 day(s), 21 crab-only of 173 sampled boats (raw share 0.121). This is a LOWER BOUND on the crabbing fraction f: OSP labels combo trips by the non-crab fishery.
params$osp_boat_series <- osp_boat   # D41 (c): the boat prep reads this, not the file again
# improvement 8: OSP crab-ONLY counts (a LOWER bound on the crabbing fraction f, because
# OSP labels combo trips by the non-crab fishery). Lifted so the boat prep and the diagnostics
# read one file read. D41 (d): the PE's crabbing fraction never reads these rows (the sampler
# contacts alone), so a boat component that reports its PE carries no OSP information into
# the port total; the comparison table says so (pe_f_source). Empty when the column is absent.
params$osp_crab_rows <- attr(osp_boat, "osp_crab_rows")
# B48 (2026-09-28): the per-day crab-only rows as the model reads them (the boats SAMPLED, the
# rate behind that n and where it came from), so the f floor can be audited day by day.
if (!is.null(params$osp_crab_rows) && nrow(params$osp_crab_rows) > 0)
  tryCatch(utils::write.csv(dplyr::mutate(params$osp_crab_rows, crab_only_share = osp_crab_only / osp_total),
                            file.path(output_dir, "osp_crab_only_daily.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
           error = function(e) cat("  osp_crab_only_daily.csv not written:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
# D39 (2026-10-19): the OSP days with boats and no crab-only value, as the reader read them.
.osp_absent <- attr(osp_boat, "osp_absent_days")
if (!is.null(.osp_absent) && nrow(.osp_absent) > 0)
  tryCatch(utils::write.csv(.osp_absent, file.path(output_dir, "osp_absent_days.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
           error = function(e) bss_warn("OSP", paste("osp_absent_days.csv not written:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"))

osp_overlap <- tryCatch(diagnose_osp_trailer_overlap(osp_boat, params, output_dir = output_dir),
                        error = function(e) { bss_warn("OSP", paste("OSP overlap diagnostic skipped:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL })
##   OSP daily total vs trailer (trailer_mean_per_visit): n=14, r=0.933, trailer = 0.286 * OSP through origin (within-day turnover ~ 3.5); on OSP-zero days the trailer is also zero 0/0. Near-proportional, so the two series can enter the boat effort model as one latent process with a fixed scale ratio: the 14 overlap days calibrate it and the trailer-only stretch carries the OSP-dark winter.
# Review item 3 + 5 (2026-09-08): resolve tau_boat_prior_mu = "calibration" from THIS
# window's overlap; the resolved number replaces the key so the PE (run_pe_gear), the
# daily-combined series, the shared-turnover prior and the tau projection agree. Mirrors
# the pooled driver. See 03_R_functions/bss_turnover_prior.R.
params <- bss_resolve_tau_boat_prior(params, osp_overlap)
##   tau_boat prior centre RESOLVED from the OSP/trailer overlap: 3.500 (trailer_mean_per_visit, n = 14 paired days; prior log-SD 0.50). The PE expands on the same value.
# B55 (2026-09-29): the L_effective regression only when a day length is used (see the
# pooled driver and bss_needs_day_length()); under gear-deployments nothing reads it.
L_eff_model <- NULL
if(isTRUE(params$use_ie_day_length) && bss_needs_day_length(params) && nrow(ie_data) > 0) {
  L_eff_model <- estimate_L_effective(ie_data, params)
  if(!is.null(L_eff_model) && !is.null(L_eff_model$detail)) {
    write.csv(L_eff_model$detail,
              file.path(output_dir, "L_effective_ie_detail.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
# --- improvement 4: opener effort covariates (gear-resolved track) -----------------
# The gear driver does not carry the pooled report's spillover section, so when the
# screen is in "auto" mode it runs the same diagnostic here (it is cheap, works on the
# in-memory dwg, and changes no estimate). Everything is guarded: a missing opener
# calendar disables the feature, never the run.
params$opener_flags <- tryCatch(opener_flag_series(params),
                                error = function(e) { message("  Opener calendar unavailable: ",
                                                              conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
opener_spill <- NULL
if (identical(tolower(params$opener_covariate_mode %||% "off"), "auto")) {
  opener_spill <- tryCatch(diagnose_fishery_spillover(dwg, params),
                           error = function(e) { message("  Opener screen diagnostic skipped: ",
                                                         conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}
opener_sel <- tryCatch(opener_select(opener_spill, params),
                       error = function(e) list(shore = character(0), private_boat = character(0),
                                                table = NULL, mode = "off", note = "screen failed"))
params$opener_selected <- list(shore = opener_sel$shore, private_boat = opener_sel$private_boat)
params$razor_dig_active <- identical(tolower(params$razor_dig_mode %||% "no"), "yes")
params$opener_f_dates <- tryCatch({
  fl <- params$opener_flags; ff <- params$opener_f_flag %||% "ma2_halibut_open"
  if (!is.null(fl) && ff %in% names(fl)) fl$event_date[as.logical(fl[[ff]])] else as.Date(character(0))
}, error = function(e) as.Date(character(0)))
message(sprintf("Opener effort covariates: mode=%s | shore: %s | private boat: %s",
                opener_sel$mode,
                if (length(opener_sel$shore)) paste(opener_sel$shore, collapse = ", ") else "(none)",
                if (length(opener_sel$private_boat)) paste(opener_sel$private_boat, collapse = ", ") else "(none)"))
if (length(opener_sel$private_boat) > 0 && isTRUE(params$use_crab_fraction) &&
    !(params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none") %in% c("opener", "month_opener"))
  message(paste0("  *** WARNING: a BOAT opener covariate is active while crab_fraction_strata = '",
                 params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none",
                 "'. Fitting the opener-day ALL-boat surge more faithfully and then multiplying it ",
                 "by a constant f converts boats we know are not crabbing into crab effort. Use ",
                 "crab_fraction_strata = 'opener' or 'month_opener'. ***"))

# --- 2026-09-25: marine hazard effort covariates (NWS SCA-or-higher, USCG bar restriction) --
# Same mechanism as the pooled driver (03_R_functions/bss_marine_hazard_covariates.R): the
# selected covariates become extra columns of the K_open block, so the gear Stan model is
# unchanged. The method of record since 2026-09-27 is "manual" with nws_sca_any on the boat,
# confined by the prep to the all-gear fit (marine_hazard_gear_regimes; A30). "off" reads
# nothing; any other mode stops on a missing or non-covering archive.
marine_hazard <- marine_hazard_prepare(dwg, params, output_dir = output_dir)
##   NWS marine hazards: 3796 event(s) with codes SC.Y/RB.Y/SW.Y/SI.Y/GL.W/SR.W/SE.W/HF.W; flags on 150 of 365 days (any zone; 51 in the winter months 12/1/2, 99 in the rest)
##   Bar restrictions: option on the form from 2023-11-18; 221 observed day(s) in the window (80 restricted), 144 imputed
##     bar_restriction: 144 unsampled day(s) imputed from logit(P) = -2.25 +1.29*bar SCA +1.38*coastal SCA +0.50*winter, fitted on 716 observed days (235 restricted) 
## Marine hazard effort covariates: mode=manual
##   definition: SC.Y/RB.Y/SW.Y/SI.Y/GL.W/SR.W/SE.W/HF.W in effect at any moment between 04:00 and 16:00 America/Los_Angeles; zones bar = PZZ110, coastal = PZZ156
##   shore: (none)
##   private boat: nws_sca_any
##   applied to the sub-season gear regime(s): all_gear
##   Marine hazard covariates forced (manual); no significance screen applied.
##   NOTE: a BOAT marine hazard covariate is active. Boat effort is ALL private boats; if crabbing boats
##         respond to an advisory or a bar restriction differently from finfish boats, the crabbing
##         fraction f differs on those days and the monthly f cannot see it. Read the boat total with that
##         in mind (CHANGE_REGISTER D30).
params <- marine_hazard$params

timer_stop("1_load_data")

2. Input diagnostics: effort, CPUE, and day length

Diagnostic views of the raw inputs before any modeling: sampled effort over the season by day type, interview CPUE, effort by month, and the I/E-derived effective day length. Healthy: effort and CPUE track the expected seasonal shape (a summer peak), with no single day dominating the series.

3. Point Estimator (PE)

The design-based estimator: it averages sampled days within each stat-week by day-type stratum and expands to the season, independently of the BSS. It is the model-free cross-check the gate can fall back to. This block also runs the commercial/charter census and the PE port totals.

The unsampled and singleton (week x day-type) cells are handled by the same three settings the pooled track uses, from one shared implementation (03_R_functions/pe_effort_strata.R, rebuilt 2026-09-12): the effort of an unsampled cell is imputed from the same day type in the same month (pe_empty_effort_stratum = "local_day_type"), its CPUE from that month’s ratio-of-sums (pe_empty_stratum = "local"), and a cell resting on one sampled day or none now contributes variance rather than the zero the retired sd()-of-one formula gave it (pe_variance = "impute_aware"); how many of this run’s days that covers is in pe_empty_effort_strata.csv (it was 44% and 43% of the shore and boat all-gear days on the 2024-25 development season). run_config.R documents each with its measured effect; pe_empty_effort_strata.csv carries the per-component numbers for this run.

# ---- 7.2 PE ESTIMATES ----
timer_start("3_PE_estimates")
message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n PE ESTIMATES\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
pe_all <- list()
for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
  for(ss in subseasons) {
    label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
    days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model)
    summ_ss <- prep_population_summary(dwg, pop, ss$start, ss$end, params)
    pe_all[[label]] <- run_pe_gear(summ_ss, days_ss, params, label, population = pop)
  }
}
## 
##   shore [2025-09-16 to 2025-11-30]: 132 effort obs, 912 interviews, crab/gear=0.76, R_G_empirical=1.31
##   PE shore_ring_net_only strata: 2 of 24 cells unsampled (3 of 76 days, 3.9%), 11 cells with ONE sampled day (22 days); fill 'local_day_type', variance 'impute_aware'.
##     imputed effort 404 of 6,394 (6.3%); SE 471 (7.4%) against 252 (3.9%) on the sampled-only arithmetic.
##   PE check [shore_ring_net_only / Dungeness_Kept]: implied CPUE 0.9498 vs interview ratio-of-sums 0.9589 (0.99x) [gear-deployments]
##   PE shore_ring_net_only: Effort=6,394 gear-deployments, Dung=6,073
## 
##   shore [2025-12-01 to 2026-09-15]: 511 effort obs, 3844 interviews, crab/gear=0.79, R_G_empirical=1.26
##   PE shore_all_gear strata: 16 of 89 cells unsampled (32 of 289 days, 11.1%), 30 cells with ONE sampled day (59 days); fill 'local_day_type', variance 'impute_aware'.
##     imputed effort 6,886 of 34,681 (19.9%); SE 2,531 (7.3%) against 629 (1.8%) on the sampled-only arithmetic.
##   PE check [shore_all_gear / Dungeness_Kept]: implied CPUE 0.4818 vs interview ratio-of-sums 0.4662 (1.03x) [gear-deployments]
##   PE shore_all_gear: Effort=34,681 gear-deployments, Dung=16,708
## 
##   private_boat [2025-09-16 to 2025-11-30]: 94 effort obs, 2 interviews, crab/gear=1.57, R_G_empirical=0.64
##   PE gear ratio arm 'match_bss' [gear-resolved boat]: 2 -> 2 interviews (matches the BSS R_G_boat frame)
##   PE boat scale: gear_per_group=3.50, tau=3.50, mean f=0.300 (deployments, crab-directed)
##   PE private_boat_ring_net_only strata: 2 of 24 cells unsampled (3 of 76 days, 3.9%), 11 cells with ONE sampled day (22 days); fill 'local_day_type', variance 'impute_aware'.
##     imputed effort 43 of 606 (7.1%); SE 167 (27.5%) against 61 (10.1%) on the sampled-only arithmetic.
##   PE check [private_boat_ring_net_only / Dungeness_Kept]: implied CPUE 1.7247 vs interview ratio-of-sums 1.7143 (1.01x) [gear-deployments]
##   PE private_boat_ring_net_only: Effort=606 gear-deployments, Dung=1,045
## 
##   private_boat [2025-12-01 to 2026-09-15]: 369 effort obs, 268 interviews, crab/gear=0.87, R_G_empirical=1.15
##   PE gear ratio arm 'match_bss' [gear-resolved boat]: 268 -> 247 interviews (matches the BSS R_G_boat frame)
##   PE boat scale: gear_per_group=3.26, tau=3.50, mean f=0.507 (deployments, crab-directed)
##   PE private_boat_all_gear strata: 14 of 89 cells unsampled (26 of 289 days, 9.0%), 29 cells with ONE sampled day (56 days); fill 'local_day_type', variance 'impute_aware'.
##     imputed effort 1,577 of 9,320 (16.9%); SE 785 (8.4%) against 579 (6.2%) on the sampled-only arithmetic.
##   PE check [private_boat_all_gear / Dungeness_Kept]: implied CPUE 1.9457 vs interview ratio-of-sums 2.3660 (0.82x) [gear-deployments]
##   PE private_boat_all_gear: Effort=9,320 gear-deployments, Dung=18,133
# 2026-08-27: the empty-effort-stratum audit as a FILE, so both tracks report it the same
# way regardless of chunk options. See write_pe_empty_stratum_report() in
# 03_R_functions/save_run_diagnostics.R.
pe_empty_report <- write_pe_empty_stratum_report(pe_all, output_dir, params)


# ---- 7.3 PE PLOTS ----
message("\n  Generating PE plots...\n")
pe_daily_all <- list()
for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
  for(ss in subseasons) {
    label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
    days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model)
    summ_ss <- prep_population_summary(dwg, pop, ss$start, ss$end, params)

    # P1: this daily PE series must use the SAME effort basis as run_pe_gear(), or the
    # daily plots contradict the totals. It previously applied the shore
    # crabber-hours formula (crabbers x day_length) to the boat as well.
    is_shore_d <- (pop == "shore")
    spec_d <- bss_effort_spec(is_shore_d, days_ss, params)
    if(is_shore_d) {
      mult_d <- if(spec_d$effort_scale_gear == 1L) 1.0 else summ_ss$crabbers_per_gear
      Lcol_d <- if(spec_d$unit == "gear-deployments") (params$tau_shore_prior_mu %||% bss_tau_fallback("shore", params)) else NA
    } else {
      ng_d   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(summ_ss$interview$number_of_gear))
      ng_d   <- ng_d[!is.na(ng_d) & ng_d > 0]
      mult_d <- if(length(ng_d) > 0) mean(ng_d) else (params$gear_per_group_default %||% 4.0)
      Lcol_d <- params$tau_boat_prior_mu %||% bss_tau_fallback("private_boat", params)
    }

    de <- summ_ss$effort_index |>
      filter(count_sequence <= params$bss_max_count_seq) |>
      group_by(event_date, section_num) |>
      summarise(mean_count = mean(count_quantity), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(est_units = mean_count * mult_d) |>
      left_join(days_ss |> select(event_date, day_type, day_length), by = "event_date") |>
      mutate(L_d = if(is.na(Lcol_d)) day_length else Lcol_d,
             est_daily_effort = est_units * L_d,
             est_daily_effort_units = est_daily_effort,   # unit is `effort_unit` below
             effort_unit = spec_d$unit,
             population = pop, subseason = ss$name)
    pe_daily_all[[label]] <- de
  }
}

##

## 
##   private_boat [2025-09-16 to 2025-11-30]: 94 effort obs, 2 interviews, crab/gear=1.57, R_G_empirical=0.64
## 
##   private_boat [2025-12-01 to 2026-09-15]: 369 effort obs, 268 interviews, crab/gear=0.87, R_G_empirical=1.15
pe_daily_df <- bind_rows(pe_daily_all)

p_pe_effort <- pe_daily_df |>
  mutate(pop_label = case_when(
    population == "shore" ~ "Shore Crabbers",
    population == "private_boat" ~ "Private Boat Crabbers")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = event_date, y = est_daily_effort_units, color = day_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.3, se = TRUE, color = "grey30") +
  pot_closure_markers(params, labels = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~pop_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "PE: Estimated Daily Effort (gear-deployments) by Population",
       x = "Date", y = "Estimated effort (gear-deployments)", color = "Day type") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_pe_daily_effort.png"), p_pe_effort, width = 10, height = 8)
print(p_pe_effort)

timer_stop("3_PE_estimates")

##     Day Type    Sampled  Calendar  Expanded-to  Vessels/day  Vessels

# --- 2026-09-13: THE CENSUS FRAME WARNINGS, IN THE REPORT --------------------------------
# Matt, on whether estimate_comm_charter() should stop rather than warn on a missing census
# frame: "a warning is fine - included in the html report." A bare warning() does not
# satisfy that: knitr defers warnings to the end of a chunk, an html_document can be told to
# hide them, and a batch runner rendering with quiet = TRUE never shows them at all, which
# is how a run whose census component is 0 because the frame is MISSING can look like a run
# whose census component is genuinely small. The conditions come back from the function as
# DATA, are printed here unconditionally, and are written to census_frame_warnings.csv so a
# verdict block can read them from the output folder without re-running anything. Identical
# block in the pooled driver; the two tracks must not differ in what they disclose.
.fw <- pe_all$comm_charter$frame_warnings %||% character(0)
if (length(.fw)) {
  cat("\n", strrep("!", 78), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(sprintf(" CENSUS FRAME: %d condition(s) that change how the commercial/charter number\n",
              length(.fw)))
  cat(" should be read. None of these stops the run; every one of them is a fact about\n")
  cat(" the FRAME, not about the catch.\n")
  cat(strrep("!", 78), "\n", sep = "")
  for (i in seq_along(.fw)) cat(sprintf(" %d. %s\n", i, .fw[i]))
  cat(strrep("!", 78), "\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("  Census frame: no frame conditions to report.\n")
}
## 
## !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
##  CENSUS FRAME: 3 condition(s) that change how the commercial/charter number
##  should be read. None of these stops the run; every one of them is a fact about
##  the FRAME, not about the catch.
## !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
##  1. ROSTER-ONLY DAYS: 2 charter trip(s) on 2 day(s) with no vessel tally. They are in the frame because charter_frame = 'roster' unions the roster with the tally; a tally-only frame would carry 0 crab on those days.
##  2. FRAMES DISAGREE on 1 tally day(s): the vessel tally and the charter roster give different trip counts. The larger of the two is used. See roster_reconciliation in census_roster_reconciliation.csv.
##  3. UNSAMPLED DAYS TREATED AS NO OPERATION: 11 calendar day(s) in the census window have no tally row, and census_expansion = 'none' records them as days on which no vessel operated rather than imputing them. That is what the tally means; it is stated here because the alternative (census_expansion = 'day_type') would add catch on those days.
## !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
utils::write.csv(data.frame(n = seq_along(.fw), warning = if (length(.fw)) .fw else character(0),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                 file.path(output_dir, "census_frame_warnings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  Component  = c(component_names, "PORT TOTAL"),
  Effort = c(vapply(component_keys, function(k) pe_field(k, "effort_total"),  numeric(1)), pe_port_total("effort_total")),   # gear deployments (census: vessel-trips); was Effort_hrs
  Dungeness  = c(vapply(component_keys, function(k) pe_field(k, "Dungeness_Kept"), numeric(1)), pe_port_total("Dungeness_Kept")),
  # D22 (2), 2026-10-19 (B73), as the pooled driver: the PE catch SE per component and the root of the sum of squares for the port
  Dungeness_SE = local({ se <- vapply(component_keys, function(k) as.numeric(if (identical(k, "comm_charter")) pe_all$comm_charter$carried_se %||% NA_real_ else pe_all[[k]]$catch_se %||% NA_real_), numeric(1))
                         c(se, sqrt(sum(se^2, na.rm = TRUE))) })
)
