14. Expansion ratios (R_G and R_G_boat)

The gear-per-crabber ratio (shore) and gear-per-boat-group ratio (boat) that carry effort onto the gear-deployment scale. Healthy: the shore R_G is data-identified (a tight interval near ~1.3 gear per crabber); the boat R_G is prior-driven (no gear counts in boat fits), so read its wide interval as expected, not a failure.

# ===========================================================================
# 7.16 R_G AND R_G_boat POSTERIOR SUMMARIES
# v5.3: Stan model now exposes R_G_boat (gear per boat group) in place of
#       R_T (trailers per group). For shore fits R_G_boat is sampled from
#       its prior but has no data attached, so it is reported only for
#       boat fits. For boat fits R_G is fixed at params$R_G_fixed_boat.
# v5.1: Notes R_G behavior for boat vs shore fits
# ===========================================================================

message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n EXPANSION RATIO POSTERIORS (R_G, R_G_boat)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
expansion_results <- list()
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$pe_fallback) || !b$pe_fallback) {
    R_G_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "R_G")$R_G

    # R_G_boat is only data-informed for boat fits; report it there.
    # F5: R_G is NEVER fixed. estimate_R_G and R_G_fixed are not declared in the
    # Stan model (rstan ignores them), so R_G is always a parameter. In a boat fit
    # Gear_n = 0, so R_G has no likelihood and simply samples its lognormal prior.
    # The old label said "fixed at 1.30", which was false.
    is_shore_fit <- grepl("^shore_", label)
    R_G_status <- if(is_shore_fit) "estimated (gear counts)" else "prior-only (no gear counts in boat fits)"

    if(!is_shore_fit) {
      R_G_boat_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "R_G_boat")$R_G_boat
      R_G_boat_median <- round(median(R_G_boat_draws), 3)
      R_G_boat_lo95   <- round(quantile(R_G_boat_draws, 0.025), 3)
      R_G_boat_hi95   <- round(quantile(R_G_boat_draws, 0.975), 3)
      R_G_boat_interp <- sprintf("%.2f gear per boat group (%.2f-%.2f)",
        R_G_boat_median, R_G_boat_lo95, R_G_boat_hi95)
    } else {
      R_G_boat_median <- NA_real_
      R_G_boat_lo95   <- NA_real_
      R_G_boat_hi95   <- NA_real_
      R_G_boat_interp <- "not applicable (shore fit)"
    }

    expansion_results[[label]] <- tibble(
      fit = label,
      R_G_median = round(median(R_G_draws), 3),
      R_G_lo95 = round(quantile(R_G_draws, 0.025), 3),
      R_G_hi95 = round(quantile(R_G_draws, 0.975), 3),
      R_G_status = R_G_status,
      R_G_interpretation = sprintf("%.2f gear per crabber (%.2f-%.2f) [%s]",
        median(R_G_draws), quantile(R_G_draws, 0.025), quantile(R_G_draws, 0.975), R_G_status),
      R_G_boat_median = R_G_boat_median,
      R_G_boat_lo95 = R_G_boat_lo95,
      R_G_boat_hi95 = R_G_boat_hi95,
      R_G_boat_interpretation = R_G_boat_interp
    )
  }
}
if(length(expansion_results) > 0) {
  expansion_df <- bind_rows(expansion_results)
  message("\n")
  for(i in 1:nrow(expansion_df)) {
    message(sprintf("  %s:\n    R_G:      %s\n    R_G_boat: %s\n",
                expansion_df$fit[i],
                expansion_df$R_G_interpretation[i],
                expansion_df$R_G_boat_interpretation[i]))
  }
  write.csv(expansion_df, file.path(output_dir, "expansion_ratios.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

15. PE vs BSS comparison

Side by side, the design-based PE and the Bayesian BSS for each component. How to read it: close agreement is reassuring; a large gap on a component means the two methods disagree there, usually because that component is data-thin, and the BSS interval width tells you how well-identified it is. Since both run on the same effort unit, a remaining gap is a genuine model disagreement, not a unit artifact.

# ===========================================================================
# 7.17 PE VS BSS COMPARISON TABLE
# ===========================================================================

message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n PE VS BSS COMPARISON (by component)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
comparison <- list()
for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
  for(ss in subseasons) {
    label_cg <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_Dungeness_Kept")
    pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
    b <- bss_all[[label_cg]]

    pe_catch <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0
    pe_effort <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total %||% 0

    if(!is.null(b) && (is.null(b$pe_fallback) || !b$pe_fallback)) {
      bss_catch <- b$C_expected_sum["50%"]   # B44: expected catch, as the pooled track
      bss_effort <- b$E_sum["50%"]
      # 2026-10-18 (D27): the columns are named for their direction, (BSS - PE) / PE; they were
      # effort_diff_pct / catch_diff_pct, unlabelled, until then (the narrative states PE relative to BSS).
      bss_vs_pe_catch_pct <- round((bss_catch - pe_catch) / pe_catch * 100, 1)
      bss_vs_pe_effort_pct <- round((bss_effort - pe_effort) / pe_effort * 100, 1)

      conv <- convergence_df |> filter(fit == label_cg)
      method <- if(nrow(conv) > 0 && conv$pass_convergence[1]) "BSS" else "PE"
    } else {
      bss_catch <- NA; bss_effort <- NA
      bss_vs_pe_catch_pct <- NA; bss_vs_pe_effort_pct <- NA
      method <- "PE"
    }
    # D41 (d), 2026-10-19, as the pooled driver: the PE's crabbing fraction never reads OSP.
    pe_f_src <- if (pop == "private_boat") "contacts only (no OSP)" else NA_character_
    if (pop == "private_boat" && identical(method, "PE") && isTRUE(params$use_osp_crab_lower))
      bss_warn("OSP", sprintf(paste0("%s (%s) reports its PE: the PE's crabbing fraction reads the sampler contacts alone, so OSP's ",
                                     "crab-only share (A33) and boat count are not in the port total for this component"), pop, ss$display_name),
               severity = "note")

    comparison[[length(comparison)+1]] <- tibble(
      component = paste0(pop, " (", ss$display_name, ")"),
      PE_effort = round(pe_effort),
      BSS_effort = round(bss_effort),
      bss_vs_pe_effort_pct = bss_vs_pe_effort_pct,
      PE_catch = round(pe_catch),
      BSS_catch = round(bss_catch),
      PE_catch_se = round(pe_all[[pe_label]]$catch_se %||% NA_real_),   # D22 (2), B73
      bss_vs_pe_catch_pct = bss_vs_pe_catch_pct,
      method_selected = method,
      pe_f_source = pe_f_src
    )
  }
}

comparison[[length(comparison)+1]] <- tibble(
  component = "comm_charter (census)",
  PE_effort = round(pe_all$comm_charter$effort_total),
  BSS_effort = NA, bss_vs_pe_effort_pct = NA,
  PE_catch = round(pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept),
  BSS_catch = NA, PE_catch_se = round(pe_all$comm_charter$carried_se %||% NA_real_), bss_vs_pe_catch_pct = NA,
  pe_f_source = NA_character_,
  # 2026-09-11: the two populations, two estimators
  method_selected = local({ .c <- pe_all$comm_charter; sprintf(
    "Commercial CENSUS %s (%s crab) + Charter EXPANSION (%s frame, %s; %.0f trips, %d interviewed, %s crab, SE %s); carried SE %s ('%s')",
    if (identical(.c$census_expansion %||% "none", "none")) "(exact over the tally days)" else "(day-type stratified)",
    format(round(.c$commercial_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ","), .c$charter_frame %||% "tally", .c$charter_expansion %||% "pooled",
    .c$charter_trips %||% NA, .c$charter_interviews %||% NA, format(round(.c$charter_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ","),
    format(round(.c$charter_se %||% NA), big.mark = ","), format(round(.c$carried_se %||% 0), big.mark = ","),
    .c$census_uncertainty %||% "charter") })
)

comparison_df <- bind_rows(comparison)
message("\n")
report_table(comparison_df, caption = "PE vs BSS by component")

# `method_selected` already recorded the gate verdict, but a rejected fit still leaves its

16. Season summary

Run-level metadata: the season window, sampling coverage, interview count, how many fits passed the gate, and the mode split, a one-page header for the run.

# ===========================================================================
# 7.18 SEASON SUMMARY ONE-PAGER
# ===========================================================================

message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n SEASON SUMMARY\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
port_total_cg <- "Dungeness_Kept"
pt_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0("port_total_", port_total_cg, ".csv"))
if(file.exists(pt_file)) {
  port_total <- read.csv(pt_file)
} else {
  port_total <- tibble(Estimate = c("Effort","Expected_Catch","Predictive_Catch"), PE = NA, BSS_median = NA, BSS_lo95 = NA, BSS_hi95 = NA)
}

mode_catch <- c(
  Shore = round(pe_pop_sum("shore", "Dungeness_Kept")),
  `Private Boat` = round(pe_pop_sum("private_boat", "Dungeness_Kept")),
  `Commercial/Charter` = round(pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0)
)
mode_pct <- round(mode_catch / sum(mode_catch) * 100, 1)

monthly_file <- file.path(output_dir, "monthly_estimates.csv")

17. Incomplete-trip treatment diagnostic (improvement 5)

Four treatments of the incomplete trips, run through the fast design-based PE. This section changes no reported number; production remains exclude. The arms and the reasoning behind each are documented in 03_R_functions/diagnose_incomplete_trips.R and rendered identically in the pooled report.

The structural point that bounds what any treatment can do: effort here comes from the gear and trailer counts, not from interviews. Interviews supply only the catch rate and the gear ratios, so every arm moves the estimate through one of those two and nothing else. gear_only is the arm with real content, because the pipeline does not currently use an incomplete trip’s fully-observed gear count for R_G / R_G_boat at all. Healthy: dropping incomplete trips raises the estimate (soaking gear reads low mid-trip); a component that moves the other way is worth a second look.

# ===========================================================================
# 7.19 INCOMPLETE-TRIP TREATMENT DIAGNOSTIC (improvement 5, 2026-08-25)
#
# Replaces the two-arm (all trips vs complete only) comparison with the shared four-arm
# diagnostic, so both tracks report the same table from one implementation. The gear-type
# CPUE comparison below is retained: it is the evidence that the bias is a soak-time
# effect (pot/trap/snare read low, ring nets do not) rather than a sampling artifact.
# DIAGNOSTIC ONLY; the production estimator is unchanged.
# ===========================================================================

message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n INCOMPLETE-TRIP TREATMENT DIAGNOSTIC\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

  sensitivity_df <- tryCatch(
    diagnose_incomplete_trips(dwg, subseasons, params, L_eff_model, pe_fun = run_pe_gear),
    error = function(e) { message("  Incomplete-trip diagnostic skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}

# Gear-type-specific CPUE comparison (shore only, all sub-seasons combined).
# improvement 1 (2026-08-25): the per-gear bias is now measured in the PRODUCTION unit,
# gear-deployments, and the old crabber-hour figure is reported alongside it. This closes
# the standing caveat that the by-gear bias magnitudes had only ever been measured in the
# denominator this pipeline's own linearity diagnostic rejects (beta_h 0.57 against 1.05).
# The SIGN was never in doubt; the magnitudes are what move.
message("\n--- Gear-Type CPUE: Complete vs Incomplete (Shore) ---\n")
shore_int <- dwg$interview |>
  filter(population == "shore",
         between(event_date, as.Date(params$est_date_start), as.Date(params$est_date_end)),
         fishing_time_total >= 0.5) |>
  mutate(
    .ng  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(number_of_gear)),
    cpue = if_else(is.finite(.ng) & .ng > 0, dungeness_kept / .ng, NA_real_),
    cpue_crabber_hours = dungeness_kept / fishing_time_total,
    has_pot      = as.integer(str_detect(gear_type, "(?i)\\bpot\\b") &
                              !str_detect(gear_type, "(?i)\\bslip\\s*ring\\b")),
    has_ring_net = as.integer(str_detect(gear_type, "(?i)\\bring\\s*net\\b")),
    has_trap     = as.integer(str_detect(gear_type, "(?i)\\b(trap|star)\\b")),
    has_snare    = as.integer(str_detect(gear_type, "(?i)\\bsnare\\b")),
    n_gear_types = pmax(has_pot + has_ring_net + has_trap + has_snare, 1L)
  )

gear_sensitivity <- list()
for(gname in c("Pot","Ring Net","Trap","Snare")) {
  gcol <- c(Pot="has_pot", `Ring Net`="has_ring_net", Trap="has_trap", Snare="has_snare")[gname]
  gdata <- shore_int |> filter(.data[[gcol]] == 1, n_gear_types == 1)  # single-gear only
  if(nrow(gdata) < 10) next
  by_status <- gdata |>
    group_by(trip_status) |>
    summarise(mean_cpue = mean(cpue, na.rm = TRUE),
              mean_cpue_hrs = mean(cpue_crabber_hours, na.rm = TRUE),
              n = sum(is.finite(cpue)), .groups = "drop")
  cpue_c <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Complete") |> pull(mean_cpue)
  cpue_i <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Incomplete") |> pull(mean_cpue)
  hrs_c  <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Complete") |> pull(mean_cpue_hrs)
  hrs_i  <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Incomplete") |> pull(mean_cpue_hrs)
  n_c <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Complete") |> pull(n)
  n_i <- by_status |> filter(trip_status == "Incomplete") |> pull(n)
  if(length(cpue_c) > 0 && length(cpue_i) > 0 && is.finite(cpue_c) && cpue_c > 0) {
    bias     <- (cpue_i - cpue_c) / cpue_c * 100
    bias_hrs <- if (length(hrs_c) && is.finite(hrs_c) && hrs_c > 0)
                  (hrs_i - hrs_c) / hrs_c * 100 else NA_real_
    message(sprintf("  %10s: Complete=%.3f (n=%d), Incomplete=%.3f (n=%d), Bias=%+.1f%% [deployments]; %+.1f%% [crabber-hours, legacy]\n",
                gname, cpue_c, n_c, cpue_i, n_i, bias, bias_hrs))
    gear_sensitivity[[length(gear_sensitivity)+1]] <- tibble(
      gear_type = gname, cpue_unit = "gear-deployments",
      cpue_complete = round(cpue_c, 3), n_complete = n_c,
      cpue_incomplete = round(cpue_i, 3), n_incomplete = n_i,
      bias_pct = round(bias, 1),
      bias_pct_crabber_hours_legacy = round(bias_hrs, 1)
    )
  }
}
if(length(gear_sensitivity) > 0) {
  gear_sens_df <- bind_rows(gear_sensitivity)
  write.csv(gear_sens_df, file.path(output_dir, "sensitivity_incomplete_by_gear.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
timer_stop("7_sensitivity")

timer_stop("6_outputs")
##   [TIMER] 6_outputs: 1.5 min
# 2026-09-04 DEFECT FIX. This was `str(params)` with its defaults, and str() truncates a
# list at list.len = 99 entries with a "[list output truncated]" line. run_config carries 120
# keys, so EVERY run_parameters.txt in this repo before this date is missing about 21 of
# them, silently. That file is not decoration: config_delta() in the batch runners compares
# two runs key by key from it, and annotate_decoupled_run.R reads run flags out of it. A
# truncated dump gives that machinery false POSITIVES (a key that scrolled off one side of a
# comparison reads as "differs") and, far worse, false NEGATIVES (a key that genuinely
# differs but sits past entry 99 in both dumps is never compared at all). The 2026-09-03 Z0
# stage reported 9 UNEXPECTED config keys on a run whose config was in fact correct; all 9
# were keys that crossed the truncation boundary when new keys were added above them.
# list.len is set well above the key count and nchar.max is raised so long vectors are not
# elided either.
writeLines(capture.output(str(params, list.len = 1000, nchar.max = 2000, vec.len = 100)),
           file.path(output_dir, "run_parameters.txt"))

# 2026-09-28 (B46): session and version capture, as the pooled driver (B1.6). A gear run
# wrote neither, so its package and Stan versions were recorded nowhere but a manifest.
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(output_dir, "session_info.txt"))
cat(sprintf("\nrstan %s; StanHeaders %s; bss_seed %s\n",
            utils::packageVersion("rstan"),
            utils::packageVersion("StanHeaders"),
            params$bss_seed),
    file = file.path(output_dir, "session_info.txt"), append = TRUE)

message(sprintf("\nAll outputs saved to: %s\n", output_dir))
message(paste(" ", list.files(output_dir), collapse="\n"), "\n")
# ---- TIMING SUMMARY ----
run_total <- difftime(Sys.time(), run_start_time, units = "mins")
message("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n TIMING SUMMARY\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
timing_df <- tibble(
  Section = names(bss_timer_log()),
  Minutes = sapply(bss_timer_log(), function(x) round(as.numeric(x$elapsed), 1))
)
report_table(timing_df, caption = "Run timing summary")

Summer-extrapolation transparency

How much of each fitted component’s BSS catch falls on days with no interview, where the CPUE is imputed by the AR process and priors rather than observed. A high extrapolated share means that component’s harvest rests on the model filling unsampled time; read it as a coverage diagnostic, not a re-estimate of the total.

Share of each fitted component’s BSS catch on days with no interview (CPUE imputed by the AR process). Across the fitted components, 55.3% of the summed BSS catch falls on extrapolated days. A high ‘% catch extrapolated’ flags a component whose harvest rests on the model filling unsampled time; shares use summed daily medians, so read as a coverage diagnostic, not a re-estimate of the total.
